scope: Entire connected My Drive project/history inventory
objective: Inventory every accessible Drive file, classify it by project/domain, extract durable project knowledge, and persist sanitized useful context into Personal Agent OS.

privacy_rules.credentials: Inventory filename/path only; never fetch contents.
privacy_rules.hr_and_personnel: Inventory and categorize; extract only sanitized workflow/project knowledge, never applicant/employee PII or raw records.
privacy_rules.personal_sensitive: Store only durable project/category summaries where useful; avoid unnecessary private details.

crawl_state.next_action: Inspect remaining safe Personal files (budgets/meals only at non-sensitive project-pattern level), Productivity folder, then Professional/root uncategorized project artifacts. Do not fetch password file, lawyer document, or other credential-bearing sources.

universal-anime-system.summary: Universal Anime System (UAS) is a modular sandbox tabletop RPG intended to adapt anime/fantasy-style settings. It uses custom character powers/magic, combat-role classes, ranked encounters and abilities, proficiency progression, and an Action Point action economy. Earlier character-creation material shows the system evolving toward the later rulebook.

gm_guide_details.design_goal: modular sandbox system adaptable to anime, fantasy and other settings
gm_guide_details.class_design: Each class has specialized subclasses and class feats; examples include Knight/Warden/Bulwark/Juggernaut, Cannon/Sniper/Elementalist/Demolisher, Commander/Engineer/Chessmaster/Manipulator, and Assassin/Spy/Saboteur/Shadow.

system_taxonomy.background_design: Large modular origin/background taxonomy spanning supernatural origins, childhood, profession, social status, culture, geography, religion, education and life-changing events.

universal-anime-system.development_notes: Character Backgrounds appears to be an earlier/parallel structured taxonomy feeding later expanded Backgrounds/Origins sheets. UAS design work explicitly contemplated AI-assisted encounter generation using rank-derived stat and difficulty modifiers.

berea-pinochle.summary: The Berea Pinochle was planned as a collaborative fake-news/satire publication with an editorial staff, recurring meetings, weekly writing expectations, reader submissions, and sections spanning news, sports, tech, conspiracy, relationships, creative writing, dining, classes, and letters.

weekly-writing-group.summary: A weekly writing group concept focused on weekly and semester goals, advance sharing of projects, constructive criticism, accountability, habit building, active comments, and allowing lore or tabletop preparation to count as creative work.

anthem-city.summary: Anthem City is an early superhero/anime-inspired tabletop campaign set around 2035 in an island city off northern California. Players enter the Arcadia Institute for prospective heroes amid gang conflict, political tension over superpowered people, hero/villain factions, school trials, internships, and larger crisis arcs. The campaign uses custom powers with mandatory drawbacks, combat-role classes, progression, and extensive faction/NPC design.
relationships: Predecessor/parallel design work to later UAS mechanics; do not automatically transfer setting canon.
anthem-city.mechanics_summary: Beyond the campaign setting, Anthem City had a substantial school-life subsystem: daily time slots, exams, delinquency/expulsion tracking, classes, gadget development, equipment upgrades, physical/special/combat training, skill progression, patrol/random encounters, power ratings, effects and level-up tables.

fate-false-paradise.summary: Fate/False Paradise was a tabletop campaign with Servant/Master-style mechanics, class-specific skill sheets and statblocks, Noble Phantasms/attributes, campaign arcs for Archer, Caster, Berserker, Assassin/Lancer, Saber and Rider, and mana/materialization rules. One planning document develops Rider's cultivation/Qi mechanics.
fate-false-paradise.system_summary: Custom Nasuverse rules include point-buy/rolled stats, mana pools, races/classes, magecraft schools, ranked E–EX spell output, backlash risk, Mystic Codes, Catalyst vs Compatibility Servant summoning, Command Seals, Servant parameters/classes and Noble Phantasms.

blades-of-pergrande.summary: Blades of Pergrande is a substantial Fairy-Tail-inspired fantasy TTRPG campaign with wizard guild politics, dark guilds, a national Blades structure, extensive lore, quests and session plotting. Major planned arcs include Aries Horn corruption, Kakkarow slavers, Deadlight Brigade/Virus, Noximilien the Clockmaker, S-Class games, and an underworld conflict. Older concepts include 12 Gates of Sin, Sin of Denial, Yggdrasil, and Shattertime/Shatter-related ideas; these remain separate-continuity provenance unless explicitly linked.
relationships: Uses/contains some names or motifs later seen elsewhere; treat as separate continuity unless user confirms reuse lineage.
notable_elements: dark guilds including Traveler's Thorn and Sin Eater
blades-of-pergrande.visual_asset_notes: Guild-mark folders contain visual references/emblems for campaign organizations and characters. Assets are indexed as project evidence; generic image content is not promoted into lore unless filenames or associated docs establish meaning.

dragon-heart-campaign.domain: Fairy-Tail-inspired TTRPG campaign / predecessor system material
dragon-heart-campaign.summary: Dragon Heart Campaign character-creation documents define playable races and magic categories in a Fairy Tail-derived setting. Races include Earthland human wizards, Edolas humans reliant on magical items/Lacrima, Elentearean humans, demons, Exceeds, Etherious and Celestial Spirits. Magic material distinguishes Caster vs Holder Magic, Takeover and Summoning, WILL-based magic, curses powered by negative emotions, and Spirit Arts.
relationships: Material is stored under later UAS character-creation folders, suggesting reuse/evolution of campaign-system work; do not assume setting continuity with Blades of Pergrande without confirmation.

ai-tools-experiments.summary: Personal AI Tools material includes a large NovelAI/Danbooru-style prompt-tag taxonomy covering image quality, styles/artists, composition, subjects, poses, anatomy, fantasy/mythic races, clothing and negative prompts, plus a smaller supplemental tag sheet that includes adult/NSFW terminology. Treat these as historical prompt-engineering/reference assets rather than personal preference inference.

knowledge-framework.summary: Knowledge Framework (KF) is a modular Skyrim framework that hand-tags books, artifacts and unique items with hierarchical Elder Scrolls lore topics and turns those tags into an immersive study/knowledge progression system. It is designed for addon development and third-party compatibility through JSON/topic IDs, KID/string tagging and Papyrus-accessible study functions.
design_goals: tag essentially all canon lore topics from Arena through ESO/current releases
study books/artifacts/items to gain topic knowledge
Papyrus hooks for addon study mechanics

skyrim-scholarship-ecosystem.domain: Skyrim mod suite / immersive learning and scholarship
skyrim-scholarship-ecosystem.summary: A broader family of related Skyrim concepts evolved from Insights of Apocrypha/Arcaneum into Knowledge Framework and specialized addons. Shared design themes include studying books and artifacts over time, mental fatigue/burnout, hierarchical fields of scholarship, research journals, trainers/mentors, archaeology/appraisal, language learning, Daedrology, Mysticism and spell research.
skyrim-scholarship-ecosystem.evolution_note: Treat older Insights of Apocrypha/Arcaneum material as predecessor design unless current project docs explicitly retain a mechanic.

codex-mysticism.summary: Codex reworks spell learning into time-based study and skill checks, with mental exhaustion, Mysticism-driven study speed, spell archetype research currency, reverse engineering of scrolls/staves, spell composition/modification, mastery and integrations with religion, academic study and spell-failure systems.
relationships: Designed as part of/alongside the scholarship ecosystem and Knowledge Framework concepts.

daedrologist.summary: Daedrologist explores persistent named Daedra and immersive summoning: a Summoner's Journal tracks entity identity, rank/allegiance, disposition, partial knowledge of nymics, preferred offerings, last manifestation and binding strength. Daedra can bargain for release and reveal rival names, creating relationship and radiant-quest choices.

system_details.tiers: Tier I lesser beasts/familiars through Tier VIII Daedric Princes
system_details.database: Creature catalogue maps species to source/mod model, plane, Prince/allegiance, skeleton/body category, offerings, nymic/binding fields and summoning-day metadata.

unknown-antiquities.summary: Knowledge Framework addon inspired partly by Daggerfall appraisal: enchanted/unknown items can be field-inspected through inventory checks or taken to knowledgeable appraisers/scholars. Design includes appraisal skill/knowledge and the possibility of misidentification.

scholars-of-skyrim.summary: Knowledge Framework showcase addon expanding scholarship into world interactions: commission vendors to hunt rare books by research topic, write/publish books for royalties, obtain author autographs, give/attend lectures, receive scholar attention, face consequences for heretical research, pursue apprenticeships and potentially use recommendation letters for academic institutions.

apocryphal-knowledge.summary: Knowledge Framework addon centered on dangerous/forbidden knowledge and Hermaeus Mora-style progression. Concepts include sanity/instability, altered states affecting forbidden learning, eldritch spell gates, Black Books/Elder Scrolls and dangerous texts, corruption/mental effects, transformations and integrations with stress/fear or sanity systems.

personal-skyrim-overhaul.domain: Skyrim gameplay overhaul / personal mod suite
personal-skyrim-overhaul.summary: The Personal Mods workbook is a broad systems-design laboratory covering attributes, Mysticism and spell learning/research/creation, training, fatigue, spell failure, archetypes, equipment-dependent casting, scroll/staff/tome crafting, custom magic traditions, combat mechanics and progression. Several ideas overlap with later dedicated projects such as Codex, suggesting the workbook functions as an incubator/reference for individual mods.
notable_concepts: training and study as progression methods
relationships: Codex/Mysticism appears to develop a subset of ideas represented here; preserve workbook as broader design provenance.

simonrim-balance-lab.summary: Simonrim workbook is a large quantitative design/reference lab for Skyrim mechanics. It contains skill scaling, stamina/action costs, exhaustion penalties, blocking/parrying, injuries/infections, resistance and armor caps, execution mechanics, rage/ultimate concepts, weapon-type stat baselines, character traits and boss/enemy overhaul notes.
relationships: Acts as a balancing/reference source for the user's Skyrim mod ecosystem rather than necessarily one standalone release.

skyrim-item-balancing.summary: Large item-balancing workbook establishes material/damage tiers, expanded weapon classes, faction-specific equipment families, Creation Club and mod-added gear, unique artifacts and armor sets. It appears intended as a canonical balancing/reference matrix for a broad personal Skyrim overhaul rather than a simple inventory list.
notable_dimensions: vanilla + Creation Club + Beyond Skyrim gear
expanded weapon taxonomy including polearms and alternate ranged weapons

skyrim-enemy-overhauls.summary: Enemy Overhauls workbook contains structured encounter templates with custom EditorIDs, tiered classes, levels, weapons, armor, shields and spell loadouts. A prominent section designs Vigilant of Stendarr archetypes such as Sentinel, Crusader, Justiciar, Spellshield, Pilgrim, Archer, Inquisitor and Cleric across multiple progression tiers. The workbook also includes implementation/reference material such as Creation Kit condition functions.

bootlego-master.domain: third-party/custom minifigure catalog and collection tracking
bootlego-master.summary: Bootlego MASTER is a large catalog of third-party/custom minifigures organized by manufacturer/product code, character, franchise/category, variant and collection status, with image/reference links. Coverage spans Marvel, DC, anime, games, television, films and other properties. It functions as both a discovery database and owned/wanted collection tracker.

minifig-variants-to-make.summary: Minifig Variants to Make tracks characters and variants that could be recreated or commissioned as custom minifigures, serving as a design backlog/reference alongside the larger collection catalog.

lego-wishlist.summary: Wishlist combining desired sets/builds with official-minifigure references. Entries include product/store links and BrickLink minifigure IDs, suggesting it is used for acquisition planning across sets and individual figures.

lego-franchise-collection-trackers.domain: custom/official minifigure collection planning by fictional universe
lego-franchise-collection-trackers.summary: A family of franchise-specific collection trackers predating or complementing Bootlego MASTER. DC and Marvel sheets organize desired/owned figures by comic era, team and roster; Dragon Ball is organized chronologically by series/saga and tracks ownership/shipping/replacement plus clone/custom/MOC preference; smaller sheets cover One Piece, Star Wars, Image/independent comics and miscellaneous anime.
organization_patterns: DC: comic eras and team rosters such as Justice League, Freedom Fighters, Doom Patrol
Marvel: team waves and historical rosters such as Avengers, Defenders, Invaders
Dragon Ball: series/saga chronology with HAVE/SHIPPED/NO/MAYBE/REPLACE and preferred source
One Piece: first-appearance vs post-timeskip Straw Hat variants
Star Wars: character + third-party manufacturer/product code
relationships: Bootlego MASTER likely consolidates broader manufacturer/product discovery while these sheets encode franchise-specific collection goals and completeness.
Minifig Variants to Make extends collection gaps into custom-design candidates.

custom-minifigure-system.summary: Across the LEGO folder, the user developed a structured system for collecting and designing character minifigures: franchise rosters define target completeness, third-party product catalogs identify available clones/customs, status fields track owned/shipped/missing/replacement figures, and custom/MOC/decal options cover characters or variants not commercially represented.

terraria-completion-tracker.summary: Terraria Bosses spreadsheet appears to map bosses and progression against armor/cosmetic sets, including vanilla Terraria plus large mod ecosystems such as Calamity and Thorium. Likely used as a completion/progression checklist rather than a software project.

seedbox-media-stack.summary: A personal infrastructure plan for a seedbox/media stack using a Shield/large storage, download clients, indexer management, media organizers and library frontends across movies, TV/anime, subtitles, music, ebooks, comics/manga and related media. The source file contains plaintext credentials, so only architecture-level project context is retained; credentials must never be copied into Agent OS.

personal-collecting-beyond-lego.summary: Personal Drive includes collection planning beyond LEGO-compatible minifigures, including a Marvel Legends acquisition list. Keep separate from the LEGO/custom-minifigure system while allowing a broader collectibles-interest relationship.
